land.text: the valley of Qin, 'modern Qingshui and Zhangjiachuan in Gansu', where King Xiao of Zhou gave Feizi a fief

The page gives Qin land only west of the Yellow River ('Between 413 and 409 BC ... Wei ... conquered some Qin territories west of the Yellow River') and promises in 770 'the lands west of Qishan'. Corrected: the Shaanxi cells of the shape, all of Guanzhong, and the western core; the Shanxi cells are cut. When Qin reached Guanzhong is on no page opened (ledger event at confidence 1). The page has no area figure.

Qi ('Following the fall of Qi in 221') is still a separate Cliopatria row to 219 and is added by the 221 ledger gain, so the shape is right for 222 and short of Qi for 221-219. The Qin dynasty row (218-209) carries the realm on.

region.text: the valley of Qin, 'modern Qingshui and Zhangjiachuan in Gansu'; Qinyi 'in the modern town of Qinting'

ledger.note: 897: Feizi receives the fief of Qin from King Xiao of Zhou. 'It is traditionally dated to 897 BC' (lead); the infobox says 'Established: 9th century BC' and 'Founded by Feizi: 860 BC?'; the rulers table gives only 'd. 858'. The page gives counties, not a boundary; the 35 km disc is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Quanqiu, 'modern Li County, Gansu'

ledger.note: 822: King Xuan of Zhou awards Quanqiu to the Qin. Table: 'King Xuan formally awarded them the territory of Quanqiu'; the page calls it a recovery of land lost to the Xirong. The 35 km disc is the researcher's reading.

About 821: Duke Zhuang moves the seat from Qinyi to Quanqiu. 'Duke Zhuang then moved his seat from Qinyi to Quanqiu'; the page gives no year (the move follows the 822 award; Zhuang reigns 821-778 in the table).

region.text: Qian, 'modern Long County, Shaanxi'

ledger.note: 776: Duke Xiang holds Qian. The capital moves there 'the following year' after 777; the page does not say how Qin got the land (lead: Qin 'originated from a reconquest of western lands that had previously been lost to the Xirong'). Counterpart named for the Xirong, who have no dossier.
776: the Qin capital moves east from Quanqiu to Qian. 'The following year, Duke Xiang moved the Qin capital eastward from Quanqiu to Qian' (after 777, so 776).

region.text: 'the lands west of Qishan'

ledger.note: 770: King Ping enfeoffs Duke Xiang and promises Qin 'the lands west of Qishan'. Infobox 'Enfeoffment by Ping of Zhou: 770 BC'; body: 'He further promised to permanently grant Qin the lands west of Qishan'. A promise: the page does not say when Qin took the land, which the Zhou dossier gives to the Quanrong from 771. Baoji is the researcher's reading of Mount Qi's west.

region.text: Guanzhong and the middle of Shaanxi as Cliopatria's 750 shape draws it; 'its Guanzhong heartland'

ledger.note: About 750: Qin holds Guanzhong. The page is silent on when Qin reached the Wei valley after 771 (it names 'its Guanzhong heartland' only in the Warring States passage); the year is Cliopatria's first shape.

region.text: 'some Qin territories west of the Yellow River'

ledger.note: 413: Wei begins to take Qin's land west of the Yellow River. 'Between 413 and 409 BC, during the reign of Duke Jian of Qin, the Wei army ... conquered some Qin territories west of the Yellow River.'

region.text: 'some Qin territories west of the Yellow River'

ledger.note: 409: the fighting for the west bank ends (the page's last year of 413-409).

region.text: 'some Qin territories west of the Yellow River'

ledger.note: 409: Qin has lost its land west of the Yellow River to Wei. The page says 'some' territories, not which; the strip within about 40 km of the river is the researcher's reading. Cliopatria's shape does not show the loss.

350: Shang Yang moves the capital to Xianyang. Xianyang page: 'was made the capital of the state of Qin in 350 BC'; 'Shang Yang designed Xianyang and in 350 BC organized the relocation of Qin's administration from the old capital Yueyang'. The Shang Yang page agrees on the move and gives 350 only for the second set of reforms.

region.text: 'the land west of the Yellow River'

ledger.note: 341: Shang Yang attacks Wei. 'In 341 BC, Qin attacked the state of Wei'; 'Gongsun personally led the Qin army to defeat Wei, and eventually Wei ceded the land west of the Yellow River to Qin'. The Wei page dates the Battle of Maling to 341 and says Wei 'eventually lost the western Hexi region'.

region.text: 'the land west of the Yellow River'

ledger.note: 328: the fight for the west bank ends in Qin's favour (Zhang Yi's campaign).

region.text: 'the land west of the Yellow River'; 'a large part of Wei'

ledger.note: 328: Zhang Yi's campaign wins the land west of the Yellow River. Zhang Yi page: 'in 328 BC he led a successful campaign against his native state, by which Qin acquired a large part of Wei'. The Shang Yang page: 'Wei ceded the land west of the Yellow River to Qin', undated; the strip is the one lost in 409 (researcher's reading).
325: Huiwen styles himself King of Qin. Rulers table: 'first Qin ruler to adopt the title of King in 325 BC' (the King Huiwen page gives no year). Same state, same colour (rule 2).

region.text: 'the kingdoms of Shu and Ba to the south, in the Sichuan basin'; Shu: the Sichuan cells of the shape

ledger.note: 316: Qin conquers Shu. 'In 316 BC it conquered the kingdoms of Shu and Ba to the south, in the Sichuan basin'; the Qin page agrees ('completed the conquests'). The split between Shu and Ba and the extent are the researcher's, from Cliopatria's shape.

region.text: 'the kingdoms of Shu and Ba to the south, in the Sichuan basin'; Ba: the east, the Chongqing cells

ledger.note: 316: Qin conquers Ba, with Shu.

ledger.note: By 315: Qin holds eastern Gansu. The Warring States page says Qin later subjugated 'almost all western territories' in 'the 4th century', with no year; recorded at the eve of Cliopatria's 315 shape.

No page opened dates or names it; kept at confidence 1 so the 326 to 315 jump is accounted for. The Warring States page says only that Qin 'had begun to take fertile land in their southwest'.

region.text: Hanzhong

ledger.note: About 312: Qin takes Hanzhong from Chu (bridge). Fx-52 (K05) re-check, 3 Nov 2026: the sentences earlier quoted here ('These two battles became known together as the battles of Danyang and Lantian', 'Qin then seized Hanzhong') are not on the King Huai of Chu page as served (about 480 words: reign 328-299 BC, the 299 hostage episode and the 296 death only), and none of the pages opened (King Huai of Chu, Hanzhong, Zhang Yi, King Huiwen of Qin, and earlier Warring States period and Qin (state)) names the battles or the seizure. What the pages do give: the Timeline of the Warring States page has '312 BC: Qin defeats a Chu army' (no place), and the Zhang Yi page has, after the deception over 'six hundred li' of land, 'Chu went to war with Qin. Qin defeated Chu and demanded a further six hundred li of land' (no year). So Qin's defeat of Chu in 312 is dated, but that Chu held Hanzhong and Qin took it then is the researcher's reading, with no dated sentence on any page: the event stays at confidence 1 (the floor) as a bridge, and the quoted sentences are withdrawn. Cliopatria's Chu never reaches Hanzhong (107 E), so the compiler finds no Chu cells to move and Hanzhong becomes Qin's from 312 either way. The -315 keyframe leaves Hanzhong out until this event.

region.text: Chongqiu of Pingyuan Commandery

ledger.note: 301: Qin and its allies beat Chu at Zhongqiu (Chongqiu). King Zhaoxiang of Qin page: 'In 301 BC' Qin, Han, Wei and Qi allied to attack Chu; the Chu army was defeated 'at Zhongqiu (重丘)' and the Chu general Tang Mei was killed. The page records a victory, not a seizure of land, and gives no location; 'seized Chongqiu of Pingyuan Commandery' is not on it (nor on the King Huai of Chu page as served, about 480 words: fx-52 K05). The gain, and the 50 km disc round Nanyang, are the researcher's reading: confidence 1. fx-54 (3 Nov 2026): re-sourced from King Huai of Chu to King Zhaoxiang of Qin.

region.text: eight Chu cities on the Qin frontier

ledger.note: 299: Qin presses Chu on the frontier (the 'eight cities'). No page opened dates 'eight Chu cities': the King Huai of Chu page as served does not have the sentence (fx-52 K05), and the Chu (state), Warring States period, Timeline of the Warring States and King Zhaoxiang of Qin pages do not have it. King Zhaoxiang of Qin page: 'In 300 BC' Mi Rong was sent to 'capture Xiangcheng (襄城)', killing 30,000 soldiers and the Chu general Jing Que; 'in 299 BC King Huai of Chu was forced to go to Wu Pass (武關) to negotiate terms with Qin' and was abducted and taken to Xianyang; he refused to cede the Wu and Qianzhong commanderies and 'was detained as a hostage'; Qin 'proceeded to invade Chu the next year, capturing 16 cities and killing 50,000 Chu soldiers' (the year is only implied, 298). The count of eight, the year 299 and the frontier band are the researcher's reading; no page opened dates them: confidence 1. fx-54 (3 Nov 2026): re-sourced to King Zhaoxiang of Qin, confidence 2 to 1.

region.text: '400 li of Hedong lands'

ledger.note: 290: Wei cedes Hedong. After Yique (293) the victories 'forced Wei to concede 400 li of Hedong lands'. Hedong is placed as south-western Shanxi round Linfen and the Yellow River bend (researcher's reading).

region.text: Anyi, 'the former Wei capital'

ledger.note: 286: Qin takes Anyi, the old Wei capital. 'Anyi (安邑) in 286 BC'; the Wei page lists Anyi as the first capital and does not locate it. Placed at Xia County near Yuncheng (researcher's reading).

region.text: 'the capture of the Chu capital city of Ying' and 'territories west of the Han River'; the new Nan Commandery

ledger.note: 278: Bai Qi captures Ying. 'Capture of the Chu capital city of Ying' with 'the new Nan Commandery'; the unification page: 'capturing the Chu capital cities of Ying and Chen' and 'forcing Chu to give up its territories west of the Han River'. The region is Cliopatria's Chu shape of 284 less that of 277, as the Chu dossier has it.

region.text: Shangdang Commandery

ledger.note: 260: Qin wins at Changping and holds Shangdang. 'Bai Qi cut off the Shangdang Commandery from the Han mainland' (262); Han's commanders handed it to Zhao; 'defeated a 450,000-strong Zhao army at Changping in 260 BC'. No page opened says Qin annexed it then; the unification page has Huan Yi 'ordered to lead an army from Shangdang' about 234.

region.text: Taiyuan and the Fen valley north of Hedong

ledger.note: About 260: Qin holds Taiyuan. After 257 'The combined forces recaptured Hedong, Anyang, Taiyuan' from Qin, so Qin held it by then; no page opened dates the capture. Year bridged to Changping.

region.text: Wangcheng, the Duke of West Zhou 'conceding all his lands'

ledger.note: 256: Qin ends the Zhou royal line. 'Overthrew the Eastern Zhou dynasty in 256 BC'; Jiu's army broke 'into Wangcheng'. The unification page says 'Qin conquered West Zhou in 256 BC' and 'conquered East Zhou' in 249: the pages disagree on the labels.

region.text: the remnant 'East Zhou'

ledger.note: 249: Qin annexes the East Zhou remnant. 'Conquered East Zhou, bringing the Zhou dynasty to an end' (King Zhuangxiang paragraph). Placed at Gong (researcher's reading); needs its own dossier.

Zheng's last shape, annexed by Han in 375

Qinyang, captured by Qin in 265 (the page gives no modern name; the disc is at present-day Jiyuan)

region.text: Han's whole shape as the han dossier draws it (han/ledger/15): the Cliopatria Han shape (-247) with Yangzhai and the annexed Zheng, without Qinyang (Qin's since 265); 'The territory of Han was reorganised to form the Qin Empire's Yingchuan Commandery'

ledger.note: 230: Qin conquers Han. Neishi Teng's army 'conquered the Han capital Zheng' within one year; 'King An of Han surrendered and Han came under Qin control'. Fix pass fx-40 (2 Nov 2026), window request R010: the region was Cliopatria's Han -231 shape (16 of the 82 cells the han dossier's keyframes hold), which left a 66-cell Han shape in Henan drawn inside Qin until the 208 restoration; it is now the region the han dossier uses for the same loss (han/ledger/15). Qin's wars of unification page, re-read 2 Nov 2026: 'conquered the Han capital Zheng (present-day Xinzheng, Henan) within one year. King An of Han surrendered and Han came under Qin control. The territory of Han was reorganised to form the Qin Empire's Yingchuan Commandery'; 'In the following year, King An was executed'; 'Qin forces suppressed a rebellion by Han loyalists in the former Han capital'.

region.text: the Zhao capital Handan and its country

ledger.note: 229: Qin attacks Zhao. 'Li Xin led two forces from Taiyuan and Yunzhong to attack Dai County'; 'Qin took advantage of the situation to attack the Zhao capital Handan'.

region.text: the Zhao capital Handan and its country

ledger.note: 228: Handan falls and the fighting for Zhao's core ends.

region.text: Zhao's core: 'Qin forces occupied Handan, captured King Qian and sent him into exile'

ledger.note: 228: Qin takes Handan and Zhao. The Qin page: 'Zhao eventually fell to Qin in 228'. Prince Jia's Dai in the north holds out to 222. Shangdang is left out (gained in 260). Cliopatria's Zhao row runs to 226.

ledger.note: 226: Qin takes Ji. 'Qin forces advanced further into Yan and conquered the Yan capital Ji'; 'King Xi, Crown Prince Dan, and the surviving Yan forces retreated to the Liaodong Peninsula'. Liaodong is left to Yan until 222.

region.text: 'King Jia of Wei surrendered and Wei came under Qin control'; the Dang and Sishui commanderies

region.text: the Chu-Qin frontier, Qinan and the Huai country

ledger.note: 224: Qin invades Chu. Wang Jian 'routed them at Qinan' (224). The band repeats the Chu dossier's.

region.text: the Chu-Qin frontier

ledger.note: 223: the war ends with Chu's fall.

region.text: 'Wang Jian conquered the Chu capital Shouchun and captured King Fuchu of Chu'; 'Chu had been completely conquered by Qin'

ledger.note: 223: Wang Jian takes Shouchun and Chu ends. The Qin page: 'Qin conquered Chu' in 223.

region.text: 'invaded the Liaodong Peninsula, destroying the Yan forces and capturing King Xi'

ledger.note: 222: Qin takes Liaodong and ends Yan. 'The former Yan lands became the Liaodong Commandery, along with Yuyang, Beiping and Liaoxi.'

region.text: 'Wang Ben led Qin forces to conquer Dai and captured Prince Jia'

ledger.note: 222: Qin takes Dai. Prince Jia 'declared himself king and established the short-lived state of Dai' after 228. The disc is the researcher's reading of Dai County.

wars.outcome: Qin defeated a Chu army in 312 BC (Timeline page, no place named); Qin's seizure of Hanzhong is the researcher's reading, not a dated sentence on any page opened. Shaoling in 311 is not on any page opened either.

wars.outcome: Qin, Han, Wei and Qi defeated the Chu army at Zhongqiu in 301 BC and killed Tang Mei; Qin took Xiangcheng in 300 BC (King Zhaoxiang of Qin page); King Huai was held hostage from 299 BC ('detained as a hostage', same page). The 'eight Chu cities' of 299 and the seizure of Chongqiu are not on any page opened (fx-54), so the zones are the researcher's reading.

wars.name: Battle of Yique and the Hedong cessions
wars.outcome: Bai Qi 'defeated the two major states at Yique' (293); Wei conceded 400 li of Hedong (290); Qin took Anyi (286).

wars.name: Qin's capture of Ying
wars.outcome: Bai Qi captured Ying and Qin set up the Nan Commandery.
wars.note: The page puts it in its 279-278 entries.

wars.name: Battle of Changping
wars.outcome: Qin cut off Shangdang from Han (262), Han's commanders gave it to Zhao, and Qin 'defeated a 450,000-strong Zhao army at Changping in 260 BC'.

wars.name: Qin conquest of the Zhou
wars.outcome: Qin took Wangcheng in 256 and the East Zhou remnant in 249.

wars.name: Qin's wars of unification
wars.outcome: Qin conquered the six states in order: Han 230, Zhao 228, Yan 226 and 222, Wei 225, Chu 223, Qi 221, and the First Emperor took his title in 221.

certainty.note: Qin's lands and the Yellow River line are known from a few sentences; the western fiefs (Qinyi, Quanqiu, Qian) are circles round named counties.
The Sichuan edge (Shu, Ba) and the Chu frontier (Wuguan, Hanzhong, Nan Commandery) are approximate; the Hedong and Shangdang frontiers follow the cessions.
The unification borders are commandery outlines the pages do not draw; the Liaodong and Wuyue edges are the softest.

notes: Wikidata Q1471995 is shared with 'former-qin' (Former Qin, 351-394 CE, a Di state in Shaanxi): a different state; this dossier covers only the Cliopatria Name 'Qin' (-750..-219). The Qin Dynasty row (qin-dynasty, -218..-209) is the empire; this dossier ends at Cliopatria's 219 handoff, with the real change as a 221 rename. Budget: 12 pages opened (5 allowed for 12 shapes). Seven of them (Shang Yang, Warring States period, King Huiwen, Hanzhong, Wei, Zhang Yi, Duke Mu) were opened for the Hexi, Shu, Hanzhong and Shanxi years and gave one dated sentence each at most; Hanzhong and Duke Mu gave nothing usable. The Qin page itself is thin on territory before 316 and has no infobox area. The big finding: Cliopatria's Qin shapes -750..-326 are misplaced. They hold the middle of Shaanxi (108.1-110.6 E) and 88 to 278 cells of Shanxi east of the Yellow River, only 83 of Guanzhong's 239 cells, and neither the capital Qian (106.85 E) nor the Qin valley (106.2 E, Gansu) nor the later capital's cell reliably. The Shanxi cells are Zhao- and Han-held in Cliopatria's own neighbouring rows and no page gives Qin Shanxi before Hedong in 290-286. All shapes to 277 are marked adjust: Shaanxi cells of the shape plus Guanzhong plus a Tianshui/Long County core, Shanxi and Hebei cut, the Hexi strip cut 409-328. Not on any page opened (so confidence 1 or no event): when Qin took Guanzhong (750 is Cliopatria's year), Hanzhong's year (312 bridged), Qin's Gansu conquests (4th century), the Qinling south, the Taiyuan and Shangdang years (260 bridged), the allied recapture of Hedong, Anyang and Taiyuan after 257 and Qin's retaking, the Sanchuan and Chenggao gains of 249-242 (Cliopatria's Han 277 cells), the capital years of Pingyang, Yong, Jingyang and Yueyang (the dot stays at Qian to 351), Qin's frontier walls, and the Zhang Yi 328 Shangjun cession by name. Date conflicts: founding 897 (lead, 'traditionally') vs 860? (infobox) vs Feizi d. 858 (table); Qin ends 221 (empire), 219 (Cliopatria) or 207 (infobox); Eastern Zhou ended 256 (Qin, Zhaoxiang pages) vs West Zhou 256 and East Zhou 249 (unification page); Wei end 225 (pages) vs 223 (Cliopatria row); Yan 226 (Ji) vs 222 (Liaodong); Han 230 (page) vs 231 (Cliopatria row ends). The Cliopatria Wei -223 and Yan -291..-223 shapes overlap Qin's -223 and -222 shapes' Hebei lands, which the Wei and Yan dossiers should resolve. Counterparts needing dossiers: shu, ba (ea-01-x, states Cliopatria lacks), quanrong, xirong, east-zhou, dai (Prince Jia's Dai 228-222, not the Eighteen Kingdoms 'Dai' row 208-204). Gazetteer names needed: Qingshui and Zhangjiachuan (Gansu), Li County (Quanqiu), Long County (Qian), Qinting, Anyi/Xia County, Gong, Dai County, Shangdang, Changzhi is in the gazetteer, Hedong, Hexi (Shaanxi) as a region. Coordinates for Quanqiu, Qian and Qinyi are county seats the pages name (Li County, Long County, Qinting), typed from the researcher's knowledge of the maps, not read from a page; the Xianyang point is the page's infobox. fx-54 (3 Nov 2026): the 301 (Chongqiu/Zhongqiu) and 299 (eight cities) Qin-Chu events are re-sourced to the King Zhaoxiang of Qin page, which dates the 301 victory at Zhongqiu, the 300 Xiangcheng and the 299 Wu Pass hostage; no page opened has 'eight cities' (confidence 1), a 306 Chu attack on Yue or Shaoling in 311.
